verdict: Eleven of the 13 findings are taken correctly and completely. Two are taken only in part, both in the documents (second reader 5 and 8). The fix also brings one should-fix problem and three minor ones. The should-fix one: the generator still verifies and counts items that the check refuses, although the spec, RESULT-WORKFLOW and the docstring now say it never does. The opposite rule does hold: an unverified item never enters at_model, stated_at_model or central_reach. Malformed shapes (a list as declaration or of, a string or 'world' as models) no longer crash or miscount; each is written unverified with 'not in the shape the check requires'. blocked() matches spec §2 and has a test. stated() no longer expands a «» definition at the top level. Both lines carry the declared mark and link the review. Items only on their row's own carrier are labelled 'On its own carrier'. The row's dependence is shown through ALONE. The review guard skips a missing review file silently, but validate() already fails it ('missing or unsafe reference'), so there is no gap there. An unreadable file is skipped, as §1 says. On the branch the 25 tests pass and the working tree stays clean; the master_laws status reads current with 0 laws not matched. I reran the second reader's in-memory build of U2's 16 records, 20 laws and 21 items from copies in the f5a-recheck scratch folder. Every rule passes except the new review guard, and statements_at_model_across finds nothing. validate adds 18 errors, all from the guard, and style.lint finds no errors. With REVIEW-U2.md as the review, the guard refuses exactly the 18 items the second reader found it never names: roles_supported_reading, roles_dependent_reading, roles_alive_reading (life-as-condition-of-life 14/15/16), transmits_at_reading (transmission-is-inheritance-and-need 16), identifies_iff_reading (learning-through-a-map-is-tracking-in-the-limit 6), verifiableBy_reading (what-a-finite-stretch-verifies 15), significant_iff_held_reading (living-significance-on-held-lives 10), significance_undetermined_reading (continuation-condition-yields-living-significance 15), only_together_reading and differenceOnlyTogether_reading (joint-difference-making 13/14), response_not_fixed_reading (what-a-pools-acts-respond-to 12), kernel_and_reading (conditions-kept-together 5), not_fixes_reading (experiment-needs-return 9), run_agrees_every_start_reading (a-code-formed-between-formations 11), living_on_reaches_reading and descent_reaches_reading (living-on-and-descent 10/11), unselected_beyond_data_reading (generalization-through-lumping 13), and renewing_not_closed (becoming-finite-horizon 8). It passes renewingAt_iff_over_all_reading, optimum_broken_reading and finite_reading_not_exact. The re-rendered pages are synthetic, adapted to the branch with 'review' on the stated_at_model entries and the branch's shape_failures applied. The lines read correctly: 20 laws are matched and laws_not_matched is 0. Mixed own+model items are labelled 'At a model' and own-only items 'On its own carrier', on all four other-record rows. One item marked unverified (descent_reaches_reading) shows no line anywhere, and the status lists it. The one exception is that grammar terms render as bare 'Becoming.«则»' (second reader 8, below). Scratch is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/4cd2c9b9-8aca-4fd1-99bb-ff1a3f9d1698/scratchpad/f5a-recheck/: build.py, render.py, run_main.py, check_rules.py, edits_rules.json, edits_bad.json, out_rules.json, out_bad.json and pages/.

new_findings.claim: Three texts claim the generator writes every item the check refuses as unverified: spec §2 ('So is an item the check would refuse: a malformed one, or one breaking its record's rules'), RESULT-WORKFLOW ('An item the check would refuse is written unverified, never counted') and the master_laws.py docstring. That is false. shape_failures mirrors only the shape and three record rules (superseded or withdrawn, theorem among its law's declarations, row on another law). It does not check: the review is a review reference; the review names the theorem; a law carrying items holds no item's row; a theorem is the declaration of one item at most, in a record or across records; the item's key set. Items that break those rules are verified and counted. An item with an extra key is not written at all.
new_findings.evidence: check_rules.py and run_main.py ran on the saved dump C-aug.pickle with edits_rules.json, output to the f5a-recheck scratch folder. The check refuses all of them: 'law 13: x.md is not a reference of role review', 'law 14: a statement at a model has exactly the keys…', 'law 15: x.md is not a reference of role review', and statements_at_model_across flags 'Becoming.Transmission.ZZ.reading: … in more than one record'. The generator printed "unverified": 0. Both ZZ.reading items (transmission-is-inheritance-and-need 15, transmission-independent-where-it-binds 13) are verified and appear in stated_at_model under law 1 of both records. central_reach counts 'stated at a represented model': 1, with both in rows. The extra-key item on law 14 appears nowhere, so law 14 is counted in `counts`. Likewise, U2 with REVIEW-U2.md on all 21 items would get 18 items refused by the check that the generator verifies and counts.
new_findings.change: In master_laws.py, have shape_failures(r, i, item, declared) also return ["its record breaks the check's rules"] when any of these holds: `review not in {x.get('path') for x in r.get('references', []) if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get('role') == 'review'}`; any law of r carrying 'statements_at_model' has a str declaration among the str `of`s of the record's items; `sum(1 for _, _, y in declared if y.get('declaration') == d) > 1`. Have it return ['not in the shape the check requires'] when `set(item) != set(AT_MODEL_KEYS)`. In main(), drop `and set(x) == set(AT_MODEL_KEYS)` from `declared`, pass `declared` to shape_failures, and build the checked entry with `x.get(k)`. The review's text is not among the hashed inputs, so leave that test to the check and say so in all three texts, e.g. RESULT-WORKFLOW: "An item the check would refuse is written unverified, never counted, except one whose review does not name it: only the check reads the review." Add a main()-level or shape_failures test for each added rule.

new_findings.claim: RESULT-WORKFLOW's new sentence 'so a statement at a model changes none of the existing counts' is false when items go on an existing law. Such a law leaves `counts` for `counts_at_model`, so existing counts fall.
new_findings.evidence: The run with edits1.json put items on existing laws 14 and 15 of transmission-is-inheritance-and-need. counts.laws went from 3749 (the repository's master-laws.json) to 3747, and counts_at_model.laws became 2, with grammar 2 and vocabulary_only 2 moved out of counts. Spec §3 is exact only because U2's laws are new ('U2's 20 laws therefore change no existing figure').
new_findings.change: In _process/RESULT-WORKFLOW.md, replace 'so a statement at a model changes none of the existing counts' with 'so a statement at a model raises none of the existing counts (a law that gains items leaves them)'.

new_findings.claim: Spec §1 says the review guard means 'the line "reviewed in" points to a review that read it'. The guard checks only that the name occurs, and on U2's data it passes three items that §6 says REVIEW-U2 did not read as they now stand.
new_findings.evidence: REVIEW-U2.md names renewingAt_iff_over_all_reading and optimum_broken_reading only in its 'How it is taken' column (findings 7 and 3). It names finite_reading_not_exact only as the target of a rename (finding 21). Spec §6 says REVIEW-U2 'read the scratch of 48 theorems, before rows 11, 14, 15, 16 and 20–24 took their present statements'. All three pass the guard in the rerun build.
new_findings.change: In F5-MODEL-STATEMENTS.md §1, replace 'so the line "reviewed in" points to a review that read it' with 'a guard against citing a review that never mentions it; that the review read the item as it stands is the landing's to ensure (§6)'.

new_findings.claim: The guard matches the theorem's last component as a word anywhere in the text, so any theorem whose last component is an ordinary English word passes against almost any review.
new_findings.evidence: Against REVIEW-U2.md, the regex in statements_at_model_errors accepts the synthetic Becoming.Transmission.ZZ.reading, ZZ.closure and ZZ.other, which REVIEW-U2 never names, because 'reading', 'closure' and 'other' occur in its prose. In the spine dump, 2214 of 18750 Becoming theorems have a one-word last component, e.g. Becoming.Run.step and Becoming.Map.Endless.generates. A code-span match keeps every current result: on REVIEW-U2 it still passes exactly the three U2 items and refuses the 18. It refuses reading, closure and other, and it keeps all three cases of test_the_review_must_name_the_theorem_it_checked.
